children: The Indian rupee was modestly stronger on Monday, unbothered by oil prices lingering near their highest levels in over a month, as the central bank persisted with its dollar-selling interventions to support the currency.
was at 94.44 per dollar, up slightly from its close at 94.4850 in the previous session.
State-run banks stepped in to sell dollars right before the local spot market opened, most likely on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India, and the sales have persisted since, traders said.
Such interventions have helped anchor the rupee over recent weeks even as markets continue to fret over energy supply disruptions due to ongoing hostilities between Iran and the U.S.

On Monday, oil prices extended gains after tit-for-tat strikes between the U.S. and Iran on vessels sailing in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude oil prices were last up more than 1% at $97.4 per barrel.
Most Asian currencies slipped while the dollar index
was perched at 99.1, with market participants keeping their eyes peeled for U.S. consumer and wholesale inflation data this week to gauge the future path of Federal Reserve policy rates.

"These data are not likely to be strong enough to see the Fed hike next week. This is a challenge to the USD’s near-term outlook with OIS (overnight index swaps) pricing about 15bps of tightening for the meeting," analysts at HSBC said in a note.
Meanwhile, the European Central Bank is widely expected to deliver a rate hike on Thursday, with markets pricing in another hike for December that would take the benchmark borrowing cost to 3%.

title: Rupee shrugs off oil strain as RBI intervention holds firm
